simple-harmonic-motion.definition: Oscillation where the restoring acceleration is proportional to the displacement from equilibrium and always points back toward it.

amplitude.definition: The maximum displacement from the equilibrium position. Measured in metres for a mass on a spring.

period.definition: The time taken for one complete oscillation. Symbol T, measured in seconds.

frequency.definition: The number of complete oscillations per second. Symbol f, measured in hertz (Hz). It equals 1 divided by the period.

angular-frequency.definition: How fast the reference-circle point turns, in radians per second. Symbol omega. It equals 2 pi times the frequency.

equilibrium-position.definition: The centre of the oscillation, where the net force on the object is zero.

restoring-force.definition: A force that always acts toward the equilibrium position, and grows as the object moves further from it.

phase.definition: Where an object is in its cycle, written as an angle. One full cycle is 360 degrees or 2 pi radians.

superposition.definition: When two waves meet, the resulting displacement at each point is the sum of the displacements of the individual waves.

node.definition: A point on a standing wave that does not move, because the waves cancel there.
